name: NORD Rare Disease Research Grants
description: NORD provides seed grants to academic scientists for translational or clinical studies that further the development of potential new diagnostics or treatments of rare diseases. Grants are awarded based solely on scientific merit as determined by NORD's Medical Advisory Committee. The program funds early-stage research across hundreds of rare conditions and is open to international researchers, making it particularly relevant for patients and investigators outside the US seeking collaborative rare disease research funding.
eligibility: Academic scientists and clinical researchers at accredited institutions worldwide conducting translational or clinical studies on rare diseases
targetDiagnosis: Any rare disease (fewer than 200,000 affected in the US)
applicationProcess: Researchers respond to specific Requests for Proposals (RFPs) published on NORD's website for named rare diseases. Applications are reviewed by the NORD Medical Advisory Committee. Awards are announced quarterly.
geographicScope: International — researchers at accredited institutions worldwide may apply
documentsRequired: Research proposal, institutional affiliation, CV, budget, IRB approval (if applicable), letters of support

name: Alex's Lemonade Stand Foundation — Travel For Care Program
description: The Travel For Care program provides financial assistance to families of children with cancer who need to travel for clinical trials, experimental therapeutics, or treatment innovations not available locally. The program covers transportation, lodging, meals, and related travel expenses, removing financial barriers that prevent pediatric cancer patients from accessing cutting-edge treatments at specialized centers across the United States. This is particularly valuable for immigrant families who may lack insurance coverage or local access to specialized pediatric oncology care.
eligibility: Pediatric cancer patients originally diagnosed before age 18, currently under age 21, enrolling in or currently enrolled in a clinical trial for active oncology treatment
amount: Up to $10,000 per family for travel-related expenses
targetDiagnosis: Childhood cancer (all types — leukemia, lymphoma, brain tumors, neuroblastoma, sarcoma, etc.)
applicationProcess: Families apply through the ALSF website or are referred by their treating oncologist. Applications require documentation of clinical trial enrollment and financial need assessment. Processing typically takes 2-4 weeks.
geographicScope: United States — travel to clinical trial sites within the US
documentsRequired: Clinical trial enrollment documentation, physician referral letter, proof of diagnosis, financial need documentation, travel cost estimates

name: Family Reach Clinical Trial Access Program
description: Family Reach's Clinical Trial Access Program provides financial support to pediatric cancer patients and their families to overcome barriers to participating in clinical trials. The program covers costs that insurance does not, including travel, lodging, meals, childcare for siblings, and lost wages. By removing these financial obstacles, the program ensures that children from low-income and immigrant families have equal access to promising new cancer treatments being tested in clinical trials across the United States.
eligibility: Pediatric patients 18 years or younger enrolled in a clinical trial in the US or US territory; household income must be within 300% of the Federal Poverty Level
amount: Varies based on documented need (covers travel, lodging, meals, childcare, lost wages)
applicationProcess: Families are referred by their child's healthcare team or social worker at the treating institution. Applications require income verification and documentation of clinical trial participation. A case manager is assigned to determine eligible support.
documentsRequired: Clinical trial enrollment verification, income documentation (tax returns or pay stubs), referral from healthcare team or social worker, proof of expenses

name: RTW Foundation Rare Disease Grants
description: The RTW Foundation funds innovative research and treatment programs focused on rare diseases, with an emphasis on accelerating therapies from bench to bedside. The foundation provides grants to academic institutions, hospitals, and nonprofit organizations working on rare disease diagnostics, gene therapy development, and clinical trials. International collaborations are encouraged, making this funding accessible to researchers and patient organizations worldwide who are developing treatments for rare conditions that disproportionately affect underserved populations.
eligibility: Academic institutions, hospitals, and nonprofit organizations conducting rare disease research; international applicants accepted
targetDiagnosis: Rare diseases — gene therapy, diagnostics, novel therapeutics
applicationProcess: Organizations submit a letter of intent through the RTW Foundation website. Selected applicants are invited to submit a full proposal. Review process takes approximately 3-6 months.
geographicScope: International — US-based foundation funding global rare disease research
documentsRequired: Letter of intent, organizational profile, research proposal, budget justification, IRB/ethics approval, principal investigator CV

name: Foundation for Rare Diseases (France) — Research Project Grants
description: The Foundation for Rare Diseases (Fondation Maladies Rares) in France supports excellent research to understand causes and pathophysiological mechanisms of rare diseases. The foundation launches 4 to 6 calls for projects per year, funding fundamental and translational research. International collaborations with French research teams are strongly encouraged. This is particularly relevant for immigrant researchers and patients in Europe seeking access to rare disease research infrastructure and funding for conditions that may be more prevalent in their countries of origin.
eligibility: Researchers at academic or hospital institutions; French teams required as lead or collaborator; international partnerships welcome
targetDiagnosis: All rare diseases — fundamental and translational research
applicationProcess: Researchers apply during open call periods (4-6 per year). Applications are submitted through the foundation's online portal. Scientific review committee evaluates proposals within 3 months of deadline.
geographicScope: France and international collaborators — must include a French research team
documentsRequired: Research protocol, team composition, budget, institutional support letter, ethics approval, collaboration agreements (for international teams)

name: New York State Refugee Health Screening Program
organization: New York State Office of Temporary and Disability Assistance (OTDA)
description: The New York State Refugee Health Screening Program provides comprehensive initial health assessments and follow-up care coordination for newly arrived refugees, asylees, and other eligible entrants. The program covers medical screening within 90 days of arrival, including physical examination, mental health assessment, TB testing, immunizations, lead screening for children, and referrals for ongoing care. Services are provided regardless of insurance status and connect newcomers to long-term healthcare providers in their community.
eligibility: Newly arrived refugees, asylees, Cuban/Haitian entrants, Special Immigrant Visa holders, certified trafficking victims, and parolees residing in New York State
amount: Free — fully funded health screening and care coordination
targetDiagnosis: General health screening — TB, immunizations, mental health, chronic conditions, lead exposure (children)
applicationProcess: Refugees are automatically referred through their resettlement agency upon arrival. Walk-in screening is available at designated health centers. No separate application is required — resettlement caseworkers coordinate appointments.
documentsRequired: Proof of eligible immigration status (I-94, visa, refugee travel document), resettlement agency referral
